name: Aggressive Primary Cutaneous B-Cell Lymphoma
aliases: Primary Cutaneous Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma, Leg Type
Primary Cutaneous B-Cell Lymphoma, Aggressive Variant

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO-EORTC Classification for Primary Cutaneous Lymphomas

criteria.description: Presence of diffuse sheets of large atypical B-cells in the dermis and subcutis
Expression of B-cell markers CD20, CD79a, and MUM1/IRF4 positivity with high Ki-67 proliferation index
Rapidly growing solitary or multiple nodules or tumors predominantly on the legs
No evidence of extracutaneous lymphoma at diagnosis
Clonal immunoglobulin heavy chain gene rearrangement supporting B-cell clonality

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of diffuse large B-cell infiltrate with characteristic immunophenotype and clinical presentation on the legs, excluding systemic lymphoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histological, immunophenotypic, and molecular findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rapidly enlarging erythematous to violaceous cutaneous nodules or tumors on the lower legs
searchTerms: fast growing red to purple skin bumps on legs

common.symptomName: Localized cutaneous pain or tenderness over lesions
Constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever and weight loss
searchTerms: constitutional symptoms like fever and weight loss

occasional.symptomName: Pruritus localized to affected skin areas
Secondary bacterial infection of ulcerated lesions

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to paraneoplastic syndromes
searchTerms: nerve symptoms from cancer-related immune effects
neurological signs due to paraneoplastic syndrome
nerve problems linked to cancer immune response

rare.symptomName: Systemic B symptoms (high fever, drenching night sweats, significant weight loss)

laboratory: Clonal B-cell population on flow cytometry
imaging: PET-CT showing localized cutaneous lesions without systemic involvement
genetic: Clonal immunoglobulin heavy chain gene rearrangement
MYC gene rearrangements in some cases
other: Histopathology revealing diffuse large B-cell infiltrate with high mitotic rate
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD20, MUM1, BCL2

distinguishingFeatures: Follicular or diffuse growth pattern with centrocytes and centroblasts
Presence of plasma cells and reactive germinal centers
Often associated with chronic antigenic stimulation
Erythroderma or patches/plaques rather than nodules

redFlags: Rapid progression of cutaneous nodules with ulceration
Failure to respond to standard skin-directed therapies
Presence of systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Grange F, et al. Primary cutaneous B-cell lymphomas: clinical and histopathologic features, classification, and treatment. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2017.
